observation: The existing scheduler runs every node preflight, then every consume, then every final once per invocation by actual object identity, rejects reentry, and retains only graph metadata. counterexamples_and_controls: A preexisting bad lower-only file or population restored by the first higher callback must fail before that callback; a post-success higher callback changing it must fail the outer final or next invocation even if an inner guard already passed.

A lane read gives correct physical after bytes but wrong historical before bytes, or wrong size, or nonphysical supplied bytes while disk is correct: reject at actual consumption; comparisonReference must independently repeat its checks.

A roster callback modifies a path retained only after the first boundary read, or creates a declared absent path after selected's inner final: combined outer final rejects. Cold existing retained drift restored on first callback must reject.

Combined wrapper inherited selected tuple misses roster-only drift; initial tuple mismatch remains opaque and roster drift rejects, while mutation after matching registration rejects rather than silently falling back.

Two independently constructed same-path frames have different readers: poison one and reject; only identical actual node reused within one invocation may deduplicate, and next invocation executes all phases anew.

A metadata callback calls the same active guard through ledgerSubject: integration must not trigger reentrant-plan failure on a valid original scenario and must still reject poisoned projected bytes; a genuinely independent nested guard must execute.

Preserve actual private terminal 70->69->68 projection checks, unknown-reader rejection, wrong-root/cycle rejection, supplied physical-before-and-after mutation, inspector poison, descriptor/tuple mutation and all original cold/late controls. Nested callback reentry through metadata projections must be eliminated by a separately proved status-only local predicate or remain on original path; scheduler running guard makes naive replacement fail.
